title: Bubble Sort
problemStatement: Write a function `bubbleSort(arr)` that sorts the given array of integers in ascending order using the bubble sort technique and returns the sorted array.
description: The array should be sorted in non-decreasing order. Duplicates are allowed.
constraints:
1 <= arr.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N^2)
Space: O(1)
outputFormat: The array sorted in ascending order.

examples.explanation: After multiple passes, elements bubble up to their correct positions.
The array is sorted in ascending order.

explanation: Repeatedly swap adjacent elements that are out of order until the whole array is sorted.

title: Anagram Check
problemStatement: Write a function `isAnagram(s, t)` that returns true if `t` is an anagram of `s`, i.e. the two strings contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies (possibly in a different order).
description: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters.
constraints:
1 <= s.length, t.length <= 10^4
s and t contain only lowercase English letters
Time: O(N)
Space: O(1)

examples.explanation: Both strings use the same letters: l, i, s, t, e, n.
The character frequencies do not match.

explanation: Count the frequency of each character in s, subtract the frequencies in t; if any count is non-zero the strings are not anagrams.

title: First Duplicate Element
problemStatement: Write a function `firstDuplicate(arr)` that returns the value of the first element that appears more than once in the array, considering the earliest second occurrence. If no element repeats, return -1.
description: When two duplicates occur at different positions, the one whose second occurrence comes first is returned.
constraints:
1 <= arr.length <= 10^5
-10^9 <= arr[i] <= 10^9
Time: O(N)
Space: O(N)
outputFormat: A single integer — the first duplicate value, or -1.

examples.explanation: 2 appears at indices 0 and 5; 3 appears at indices 2 and 4. Since 3's second occurrence (4) is before 2's (5), the answer is 3.

explanation: Scan left to right and insert each element into a set. The first element already present in the set is the answer.
